references.text: The rumor about Jesus spread throughout the whole region around Galilee, a parallel to how the rumor of the raising in Nain spread throughout Judea and the surrounding area.
Here too, the expression is used that the rumor about Jesus went out to all places in the surrounding region, with the same wording (ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος / ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος).
The rumor about Jesus spread throughout Syria, parallel to how the rumor of the raising spread throughout Judea and its surroundings.
The rumor about Jesus (after a miraculous event) went out through all that country, corresponding to the spreading of the rumor in Luke 7:17.
The rumor about Jesus spread even further, so that large crowds gathered to hear him. The same pattern of the word about Jesus spreading.
The immediate context: the raising of the widow's son at Nain, which is the event the rumor in verse 17 refers to.
Elijah raises the widow's son at Zarephath, an Old Testament parallel to the raising at Nain. The rumor about the prophet's power is thematically connected.
Elisha raises the Shunammite's son. Another Old Testament parallel to the raising of the dead that confirms the prophet's God-given authority.
Jesus himself refers to the dead being raised, as part of the signs that are to be reported to John. The rumor from verse 17 is the background for why John's disciples came to Jesus.
Paul quotes Psalm 19:5 about how the message has gone out over all the earth – a parallel theme concerning the spreading of God's word throughout the region.
